movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 25 -> column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 3 bps in FY26 to 2.05% from 2.08% in FY25 (results book KPI table p28 and appendix p100; corroborated in the FY25 book p100 and the results presentation p60). The bank states the decrease was driven by asset pricing (-5 bps, competition) and growth in liquid assets, partly offset by capital/replicating (+5 bps) and portfolio mix (+2 bps). Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, the bank says NIM was stable. The results book's NIM walk (p28) is the primary framing: Liquids -3, Asset pricing -5, Funding costs 0, Portfolio mix +2, Basis risk 0, Capital Replicating +5, Treasury & Markets -2, summing to -3 bps.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Decreased margin by 5 bps driven by home lending pricing (down 4 bps) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 bps), primarily reflecting the impact of competition. The presentation splits this as home loan competition -3, cash rate lag -1, business & Insto lending -1.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Growth in liquid assets reduced margin by 3 bps; the bank notes these have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, so excluding them NIM was stable. The presentation splits Liquids & repos as increase in liquid assets -3 and increase in institutional repos -1.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Increased margin by 5 bps driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 bps) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 bps).

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Increased margin by 2 bps driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Decreased margin by 2 bps due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: The bank states funding costs were flat, contributing 0 bps to the NIM movement.

drivers.narrative: The bank states basis risk was flat, contributing 0 bps to the NIM movement.

notable_items: Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable.

disagreements.topic: NIM walk bar split between results book and presentation
disagreements.explanation: Both walks sum to the same -3 bps total but group the bars differently: the results book splits Liquids (-3) and Treasury & Markets (-2) separately, while the presentation combines Liquids & repos (-4) and Treasury & Markets (-1). The results book framing is adopted as primary per walk-preference rules.

limitations: The results book and presentation publish the same -3 bps NIM walk but split the bars differently (Liquids -3 vs -4; Treasury & Markets -2 vs -1). The results book framing is adopted as primary; the presentation's split is reported as a disagreement.
The bank qualifies the Liquids bar as having broadly neutral impact on net interest income, so the -3 bps is a margin-only effect, not an earnings effect.
No cash/statutory label is printed on the Group NIM row; it is reported on the bank's primary basis.
Capped at 80: funding +0 bps, basis_risk +0 bps. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
